OpenAI recently updated the redesigned ChatGPT Mac app, making it easier for users to access their conversation history again. Here are the details.

OpenAI is tackling major complaints after a chaotic overhaul of its Mac app

Last Thursday, OpenAI launched a new version of the ChatGPT Mac app, integrating ChatGPT, Codex and the newly announced Work agent under a single interface, while renaming the old app to ChatGPT Classic.

This change sparked controversy for two main reasons: first, the new app replaced the native Mac client with a bloated Electron-based application; second, the interface was confusing, featuring a prominent toggle dropdown to switch between Codex and Work, while the standard Chat experience was demoted to an inconspicuous button that merely opened a floating window with no access to users' existing conversation history or Projects.

Following the update, users flooded OpenAI's Community forum and social platform X to express their dissatisfaction with the chaotic redesign. The next day, Thibault "Tibo" Sottiaux, who has been leading the effort to merge ChatGPT and Codex into a unified "super app" at OpenAI, acknowledged the criticism and promised to restore conversation history and Projects to the sidebar, clarify the distinction between ChatGPT Work and Codex, and address other usability issues.

OpenAI has now updated the new ChatGPT app in response to some of the complaints, the most notable being the inability to directly access conversation history. Users can now use a prominent toggle at the top of the window to switch between Chat and Work, and use a dropdown in the sidebar to select regular ChatGPT or Codex.

9to5Mac take

Although the ChatGPT app's interface remains confusing, users who simply open the app to use ChatGPT can finally chat with the bot just like before.

However, this baffling botched launch — demoting ChatGPT to a secondary position beneath Work and Codex, coupled with the switch to Electron — suggests that OpenAI seems more focused on competing with Anthropic than delivering a polished experience for users. Fortunately, ChatGPT Classic is still around, and as long as it remains unreplaced, users can still use it.
